quote: POL in nursing practice is the action of influencing public debate regarding policy making processes by maintaining dynamic (social) networks, having a high sense of systemness, and being (clinically) credible, altruistic and accessible to peers and a wide variety of stakeholders

Conceptual clarity of Public Opinion Leadership (POL) in nursing practice is needed to provide attributes, antecedents and consequences for nurses and nurse leaders so they can contribute in the public debate and policy making processes.
Other literature would describe such knowledge, skills, and expertize of nurses as local opinion leadership (LOL) ( Flodgren et al., 2019 ).

Surrogate terms are synonymous and interchangeable with the concept of interest ( Rodgers, 2000a ).
Related terms refer to “concepts that bear some relationship to the concept of interest but do not seem to share the same set of attributes”
Credibility refers to public opinion leaders using their often extensive, clinical background to influence policy-making processes
Altruism refers to the principle and moral practice of doing something for someone else—the opposite of selfishness.

Sense of systemness refers to the multiple dimensions and nuanced perspectives that surround the whole system of healthcare and its political positions and policy-making processes, without the boundaries of a single institution

Five studies and the panel discussion identified dynamic networking as a key attribute, which relates to informally well-connected individuals who involve representative stakeholders to help improve care in the complete healthcare system
The open fishbowl method was used to structure the panel discussion; a method frequently used to enhance medium to large group discussions ( Flor et al., 2013 ).
